RSI-Scientist v0 · Proposed experiment

Can an AI scientist improve its experimental strategy?

Test whether structured memory improves evidence gathering, then test whether an updated strategy transfers to new tasks.

Status: design stage. No experiments have been run and no improvement is claimed.

Research question

Under the same model and resource limits, does a structured experiment ledger help an agent reach more reliable conclusions with fewer redundant experiments? Does a strategy extracted from that experience improve performance on unseen task families?

Three initial conditions

ConditionWhat changes
A · Fixed planThe agent specifies its experiment sequence before seeing results. It may summarise the resulting evidence at the end.
B · Adaptive loopThe agent chooses subsequent experiments using prior results in an ordinary transcript.
C · Structured memoryThe same adaptive loop records hypotheses, predictions, evidence, failed attempts and next-test rationales in an explicit ledger.

All conditions receive the same tools, data access and budget. A versus B tests adaptivity; B versus C tests the memory package. Individual memory and reflection components would require later ablations.

Evidence before implementation

The candidate task is auditing encoded-hint influence in a human–AI complementarity dataset. Before using it, establish what the labels mean, preserve treatment/control pairing and hold out entire question families. A detectable hint does not establish that it caused a model’s answer.

A controlled task with planted, independently verified effects can calibrate the evaluator before any claims are made on the real dataset. Real-data conclusions without a reliable causal label should be scored as supported, contradicted or unresolved against the available evidence.

What to measure

The primary endpoint is the number of distinct, preregistered claims correctly resolved on held-out evidence at a fixed budget. Report false supported claims alongside it. Secondary measures cover redundant experiments, execution failures, appropriate abstention, latency, tokens and cost.

The transfer test

After development, freeze the proposed strategy update. Compare the updated policy with the original policy on unseen tasks, with fresh memory and equal budgets. Successful within-task iteration alone is insufficient evidence of strategy improvement.

First pilot

A provisional debugging pilot uses three independent task families, three random seeds, three conditions and at most eight experiment slots per run. This is a feasibility check, not a powered confirmatory study. Model identity and monetary limits must be fixed before live calls begin.

The immediate dependency is a repository, schema, representative records and ground-truth definition for the chosen task.
